summary.prose: Review each task against one submitter-pinned final code revision while retaining the original commit selections as immutable scope provenance. Derive a bounded final-code view, account explicitly for surviving, superseded and deleted selections, and reject ambiguous or out-of-set changes. Reuse the current review coordinator and source readers; the other three code-review reliability fixes remain separate.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Fix approved ISSUE-599f1d0bd42e0c37: the submitter explicitly pins one final reviewRevision (user confirmed). Keep original commit selections as scope provenance and review final projected code, never generic HEAD changes. Reuse existing task-review framework. Other approved reliability issues stay separate.

api.signature: prepareReviewPacket(input: unknown, sources: ReviewSources, historical?: boolean, route?: StoryRoute, stored?: StoredDerived): Promise<PreparedReviewPacket>

parameters.name: input
parameters.purpose: Existing untrusted packet; new starts require reviewRevision, a full commit object ID. Original reviewSet and after-block/deletion selections remain mandatory. [[c2]] [[c3]]

parameters.name: sources
parameters.purpose: Existing daemon-owned committed object/diff adapter; add explicit ancestor validation using the existing typed Git merge-base tool. No direct shell, checkout, HEAD or cloud access. [[c3]] [[c4]]

parameters.name: historical, route, stored
parameters.purpose: Preserve route-correct document reads and immutable stored-history decoding. Historical read permission never authorizes old unpinned model execution. [[c3]]

returns.meaning: Validated original selections plus a bounded final-revision projection and origin-complete effective task input. No model call during preparation. [[c3]]

errors.condition: Missing/unavailable reviewRevision, non-ancestor origin, unverified original selection, unsafe path/rename, projection ambiguity, out-of-set replacement or bounds overflow. Refuse before admission/model dispatch. [[c2]] [[c3]]

preconditions: Keep existing strict original hunk/parent/path/document validation. Require each origin commit to be an ancestor of or equal to the pinned final revision. Packet array order never establishes ancestry. Never infer or substitute HEAD. [[c2]] [[c3]] [[c4]]
postconditions: Project each explicitly selected original +/- span or deletion anchor using committed path/line lineage into reviewRevision. All resulting finding coordinates and embedded reviewed text refer to that revision. Preserve every origin selection as surviving, superseded or deleted, including partial supersession. Keep one stable preparation entry per original file selection so attribution indexes remain accountable. [[c1]] [[c3]]

Unchanged text outside selected spans may shift offsets but never becomes selected. Replacement/deletion of selected material is accepted only when covered by other submitted origin selections projected to the same final scope; otherwise reject scope_conflict. Superseded origins carry trace metadata and no historical code as active finding scope. Never silently drop required modules or expand to a whole file because effective spans are empty. [[c1]] [[c3]]

Validate actual selected rename links with Git objects, preserve previousPath provenance and map to the final path. Refuse ambiguous/colliding/unselected rename paths rather than guessing. Merge-resolution text must be explicitly represented in the submitted review set if it replaces selected text. [[c3]] [[c4]]

api.name: projectReviewScope (proposed private helper)
api.signature: projectReviewScope(origins: readonly SelectedChange[], reviewRevision: string, sources: ReviewSources): Promise<ReviewProjection>

parameters.name: origins
parameters.purpose: Already-validated original selections, never untrusted raw final coordinates. [[c3]]

parameters.name: sources
parameters.purpose: Bounded committed object and zero-context changed-run reads. Existing identical blob OIDs imply identity mapping without requesting a diff that requires textual changes. [[c4]]

returns.meaning: Final paths/blobs, projected after spans/deletion boundaries and complete origin-disposition ledger derived from immutable input. Private derived state, not a second caller-authored change set. [[c3]]

errors.condition: A final replacement is not justified by submitted origins, a partial changed run cannot be mapped unambiguously, or any explicit byte/range/object bound would be exceeded.

preconditions: Operate serially through existing ReviewSources and typed Git tools. Bound work before allocating model context; do not add a generalized graph or dependency service. [[c4]]
postconditions: Treat original line intervals as sets of surviving subintervals: unchanged runs retain text with the exact line offset derived from preceding +/- counts; overlapping changed runs split the interval into surviving and superseded portions. Map only unambiguous deleted boundaries as anchors, including line zero for an empty file. Coalesce overlapping final spans while retaining all source origin IDs. Verify each projected span is within the final decoded UTF-8 blob. [[c3]] [[c4]]

Track superseded portions separately; require their replacement spans/deletion boundaries to have submitted-origin witnesses in the final projection. If overlapping partial replacement or rename cannot be proved, fail closed. No heuristic text matching, fuzzy relocation, graph inference or invented scope. Process the entire origin set before deciding whether a superseded portion has a valid replacement witness. [[c3]]

For an origin that leaves no final code, retain an explicit no-finding-scope disposition; this is not an empty segment list that permits whole-file findings. The task still assesses its acceptance checks against final code/context and remaining selected origins. Pure deleted-file/anchor scope retains current deletion semantics and committed evidence. [[c3]] [[c5]]

Projection retains each original SelectedChange unchanged and returns the exact ReviewProjection/ProjectedEntry/OriginDisposition fields in the data model. Superseded sourcePart partitions require strictly later ancestor-verified witness origins; reject witness cycles or unknown/out-of-range indexes. The deterministic identity covers final blob IDs and normalized full projection, not unpinned working-tree content. [[c3]] [[c4]]

dataModelChanges.details: Required full Git OID on every new submission; optional only in immutable historical storage decoding. The submitter pins it before start, and exact replay includes it. All origin commits must be reachable ancestors/equal. It is a source version, not a generic diff boundary or permission to review unrelated code. [[c2]] [[c3]]
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: PacketSchema adds required reviewRevision: existing oid schema; StoredPacketSchema retains optional reviewRevision for historical reads. ReviewPacket type represents both; preparation explicitly narrows new execution to a required pin. No caller-supplied final projection is accepted.

dataModelChanges.details: Proposed private prepared-state representation. Packet owns exactly one final revision; it owns 1..10000 original file-selection entries. Each original segment has one disposition with 0..many surviving final spans, 0..many explicit superseded portions, and/or deletion-anchor witnesses. Final spans may have multiple originating selections; origins remain identifiable by stable reviewSet/file/segment indexes. Direction is origin -> final projected scope, never a copied historical result body. Entirely superseded entries stay in attribution with findingScope='none'. Preserve all originals byte-for-byte in submitted history; derived projection is reproducible from their committed objects. [[c3]]

Reuse 4 MiB packet JSON cap, existing 10000 file/segment selection caps and 2 MiB per Git diff cap. Add named internal budgets capped at 10000 distinct object/diff reads and 100000 projected fragments per preparation; fragments coalesced without losing origin IDs. Bound decoded source bytes cumulatively to 64 MiB before prompts; failures explicitly refuse preparation with no model dispatch, checkpoint replacement or truncation. No hosted/provider call is parallelized. [[c2]] [[c3]] [[c4]]

dataModelChanges.entity: Saved attempt and CR version provenance
dataModelChanges.details: An attempt owns one immutable submitted reviewRevision, original selection and final-view identity. Permanent records retain the pin and original selection provenance. Old completed no-pin attempts remain historical; no auto-upgrade, mutable origin rewrite or stale result reuse is allowed. Compare final blob IDs and projected task scope with pinned requirements/tests before reusing results across attempts; unrelated revision changes can reuse only when this complete task identity remains equal. [[c5]]

errorCases.detection: New PacketSchema omits reviewRevision, uses a symbolic ref, unavailable object or non-commit OID. [[c2]] [[c4]]
errorCases.response: Reject before admission/model dispatch. Never substitute HEAD, a document commit, latest origin commit or the working tree. User resubmits an explicit committed pin.
errorCases.userImpact: No accidental review of moving or unrelated code.

errorCases.scenario: Origin is not an ancestor of final revision
errorCases.detection: Existing committed-object reads and proposed isAncestor return a valid false ancestry result; source errors remain distinct. [[c4]]
errorCases.response: Reject scope_conflict and retain stored history. The submitter must choose a coherent revision and review set; do not reorder commits or silently drop the conflicting origin.
errorCases.userImpact: No mixed-branch code assembled into a fictitious final state.

errorCases.scenario: Selected material overwritten by an unsubmitted change
errorCases.detection: Projection finds replaced/deleted selected portions without a final replacement/deletion witness from the submitted origin set. [[c3]]
errorCases.response: Reject scope_conflict. Do not add replacement lines or ignore the original module. Require a corrected explicit packet or a pin that excludes that interference.
errorCases.userImpact: Change scope remains caller-controlled even when unrelated work exists in the same file.

errorCases.scenario: Ambiguous mapping, rename or merge resolution
errorCases.detection: Partial overlapping changed runs, path collisions, unverified rename links, binary/non-UTF8 source or conflicting merge text cannot form a unique bounded mapping. [[c3]] [[c4]]
errorCases.response: Fail preparation explicitly with the affected original selection identity. No fuzzy matching, whole-file fallback, context-as-scope or partial success. Non-textual selections keep explicit unsupported mandatory evidence instead of invented textual scope.
errorCases.userImpact: Uncertain scope cannot produce a false completed review.

errorCases.detection: Packet, object-byte, diff, read-count or fragment budget would be exceeded; Git tool reports truncation. [[c2]] [[c3]] [[c4]]
errorCases.response: Reject projection_limit before model execution or checkpoint replacement, preserving all prior bytes. Submitter may provide a smaller explicit review unit. Never truncate selected code or provenance.
errorCases.userImpact: Large legitimate scope needs explicit resizing rather than silent omissions.

errorCases.scenario: Historical result or replay is incompatible with the final view
errorCases.detection: Pin changes on an exact replay, no-pin execution/resume is requested, or reused results have different final blobs/projected scope/documents/tests. [[c2]] [[c5]]
errorCases.response: Conflicting replay is rejected; a changed pin requires a new attempt. No-pin history remains readable but cannot launch a model or claim final-version equivalence. New attempts reassess incompatible tasks and preserve earlier feedback.
errorCases.userImpact: Prior approvals/results cannot silently apply to different code.

errorCases.detection: Result scope validation compares locations only to active final projected spans/deletion anchors, never superseded-only rows. [[c5]]
errorCases.response: Retain strict scope rejection; point to the pinned final scope. Bounded rejection recovery itself belongs to ISSUE-81e68ebf54745c75, not this fix. Do not auto-relocate the finding or broaden scope.
errorCases.userImpact: An obsolete location cannot remain a current blocking finding.

edgeCases.input: An early task introduces a defect and a later selected commit fixes it
edgeCases.expected: All tasks see the fixed final version; original selections remain accounted for, and a historical-only defect is not an unresolved finding. Separate genuinely missing current tests still produce findings. [[c1]]

edgeCases.input: Unrelated commits shift lines before a selected function without changing it
edgeCases.expected: Project the selected surviving lines with exact offsets; exclude unrelated added lines and avoid HEAD. [[c3]]

edgeCases.input: A selected function is partially superseded by a later selected edit
edgeCases.expected: Retain surviving subspans plus explicit superseded portions, with final replacement witnesses. Account for both original entries without duplicate model-visible code or silent scope loss. [[c3]]

edgeCases.input: Selected file is renamed or deleted
edgeCases.expected: Verify declared selected path lineage; use final path/deletion anchors and preserved origin references. Entirely superseded rows have no finding scope, never an unconstrained empty selection. [[c3]]

edgeCases.input: Same source region appears in multiple task commits
edgeCases.expected: Coalesce final text spans while retaining all origin IDs and per-task attribution. Multiple tasks may inspect the same final region without seeing obsolete code versions. [[c3]] [[c6]]

edgeCases.input: Final pin equals an origin commit; selected region is unchanged at final
edgeCases.expected: Identical blobs use identity mapping; do not call a diff reader that rejects unchanged files. No whole-file scope is invented. [[c4]]

edgeCases.input: Other code-review issue or another review runs concurrently
edgeCases.expected: Use the existing per-review fences and serial provider calls; do not change retry/activity policy or another review's state. Separate approved issues stay out of this design. [[c1]]

migration.stateBefore: s1 profiles and direct source checks show original commit-specific after-blocks feed attribution and task prompts, with no required final revision. Stored attempts and CRs preserve those pinned packets. The observed S3 review consequently retained a historical blocker despite a later included fix. [[c1]] [[c3]] [[c6]]
migration.stateAfter: Every new review explicitly pins reviewRevision and uses validated final projected scope for task source and finding coordinates. Original selections, prior attempts and completed historical records remain immutable. No model executes an unpinned historical attempt, and no HEAD default or compatibility engine is available. [[c1]] [[c2]]

migrationSteps.action: Extend contract/preparation and readers with explicit pin plus derived final-scope metadata, keeping old completed history readable. Update new-packet fixtures, producers, MCP schema and guidance together. Before any newly formatted attempt is admitted this source change can be reverted.

Qualify origin projection, stale-version reproduction, routes, historical reads, freshness and negative boundaries using disposable fixtures. Ship daemon and packet producer updates as one coordinated version change; do not introduce a runtime activation or compatibility flag.

Admit new explicitly pinned attempts only after the updated daemon is deployed. Preserve all previous records without backfill. After new-format state exists, a blind downgrade is unsafe because old strict readers may reject the added fields; retain the updated reader or use an explicitly planned operator rollback without deleting/reinterpreting records.

migration.backwardCompat: New starts intentionally require the explicit pin and reject old producer input with an actionable validation error. Existing completed attempts remain read-only historical evidence and can be republished without rewriting or claiming a final-version pin. Interrupted unpinned work requires a new explicit pinned attempt; no silent migration, old execution fallback, compatibility flag or automatic history rewrite. Existing in-flight sessions finish on their original daemon before coordinated restart; new semantics apply only to newly admitted pinned attempts.

alternativesConsidered.name: Pinned final revision with host-validated origin-preserving scope projection
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Pin one final code revision and project submitted changed segments into it, preserving their original commit provenance.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add an explicit final reviewRevision to new packets. Validate submitted origin segments exactly as today, then derive only their surviving final-version spans and justified supersession/deletion markers from bounded committed Git evidence. All reviewer tasks inspect that final view; historical origin records remain traceable and immutable. A later submitted fix supersedes an earlier defective version instead of leaving a historical defect blocking. Refuse ambiguous lineage or interference that cannot be justified within the submitted change set; never add HEAD or unrelated changes. Reuse current packet/source reader, task attribution, policy, result validation, checkpoint and CR mechanisms.
pros: Host can enforce one final code version without abandoning the caller-supplied scope.
Preserves every original selection as surviving, superseded or deleted; does not silently drop modules.
Both reviewer parties receive identical final code and origin references.
cons: Requires bounded line-range and deletion-anchor projection plus rename/ancestry edge-case tests.
Historical stored attempts must remain immutable while new input becomes explicit.

alternativesConsidered.name: Pinned final revision as reviewer-only reconciliation context
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep historical task versions as finding scope and ask the reviewer to check the final pinned code before filing findings.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a pinned final reviewRevision as context, retain current historical selectedCode blocks and validators, and strengthen shared prompts to reconcile later submitted fixes before reporting defects. No host projection changes finding coordinates or scope; the reviewer decides which historical observations remain true at the final revision.
pros: Smaller implementation in packet validation and prompts.
Retains existing result coordinates and source selection representation.
cons: Host still accepts locations against different historical versions of the same file.
Repeats the semantic ambiguity that caused the observed false block; behavior depends on prompt compliance.
Final-code line movement and superseded findings cannot be enforced consistently.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smaller, but retains the cause of the observed stale-version failure and inconsistent coordinates.
